newsitem.title: FRANCE: France urges end to Mideast tensions over water.
newsitem.headline: France urges end to Mideast tensions over water.

text.p: French Environment Minister Corinne Lepage called on Tuesday for an end to confrontation between Arab states and Israel over the sensitive issue of scarce water resources.
Speaking to the concluding session of a Euro-Mediterranean conference on water resources, Lepage said: "We must not allow water, our common wealth, to become a factor of division.
"Despite the obvious difficulties, the logic of cooperation and peace will, I am convinced, replace that of confrontation. The will to share and for solidarity will prevail," she said.

Professor Riyad el-Khoudary, head of the Palestinian delegation, told reporters on Monday that Israel was stealing water from Arab lands and he planned to raise the issue when he addressed the conference on Tuesday.
His speech was scheduled to take place later behind closed doors.
"We will certainly bring up what is the veritable theft of our water by the Israelis," Khoudary said.

"They are pumping our water from areas alongside the border with the result that about 30 percent of the water used in Israel comes from Arab sources -- mostly from Palestinian areas but also from Syria and Lebanon."

Delegates from both Israel and Syria are at the conference, the first such joint appearance since the election victory in May of hardline Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and subsequent heightened tensions in the region.
The two countries have waged wars in the past over control of water resources and a common saying in the area is that the next Middle East war will not be over oil but over water.

Yoel Guilatt, deputy head of the Israeli delegation, told reporters Israel was already cooperating with Jordan on common use of water. It hoped talks with Palestinians would also aim at projects of mutual interest, such as desalination plants, that might help the entire region.
But Khoudary complained that Israel was taking more than its fair share of water.

"In the Gaza Strip, a few thousand Israeli settlers use between five and 20 million cubic metres of water a year while the rest of the population -- a million Palestinians -- must make do with 110 million cubic metres," he said.
Attending the meeting are representatives of all 15 European Union countries and 12 North African and Middle East states.

Irish Secretary of State for the Environement Bernard Allen, representing the Irish presidency of the European Union, said demands on water resources were at unprecedented levels because of the intensification of agriculture, population growth and higher expectations on living standards and health.
The conference, which was told demand for water had doubled this century, is expected to adopt a series of recommendations on how to deal with the new problems.
